references.text: The promise of a land flowing with milk and honey was given to Moses at the burning bush, which Datan and Abiram here accuse Moses of failing to fulfill.
The description of the promised land flowing with milk and honey, which the rebels claim they were never led into.
The spies confirmed that the land truly flowed with milk and honey, but the people refused to enter.
The people's earlier rebellion against Moses and desire to return to Egypt, a similar attitude shown by Datan and Abiram.
The law about gouging out eyes refers to the same Hebrew expression for 'gouging out eyes' used here.
Samson had his eyes gouged out, using the same Hebrew expression for blinding someone.
The context in which Datan and Abiram refused to come to Moses and began their accusation against him.
